route: 5 (published subscale/block structure) + 3 (published CFA fit reproduced) + 1 (published per-item factor loadings, Fig 1)
evidence: Code derivation is core-model pattern 1 (data/lorenz_2016_psycap.py melts the S1 Dataset keeping the deposit's own column names), but the names are bare ordinals, so no data_labels exemption is available and three routes were run instead (verify_lorenz_2016_hope.R, VERDICT: PASS). (A) INSTRUMENT: the six hope columns give M=4.2497 and alpha=0.8416 against Table 1's Hope row 4.25 / .84. (B) SUBSCALE SPLIT: of the ten possible 3-3 splits of the six columns, 135|246 -- the SHS's published pathways (1,3,5) / agency (2,4,6) structure -- is decisively best: within-minus-between correlation gap 0.1466 against 0.0307 for the next best (123|456), CFI 0.990 against 0.931, RMSEA 0.045 against 0.122, scaled chisq 13.27 against 41.66-51.18 for the other nine. So the columns preserve the instrument's odd/even numbering. (C1) CPC-12 TRIPLE: the S1 Appendix names CPC-12 items 1-3 as SHS1, SHS4, SHS5. Refitting Table 2's published 4+g CFA over all 20 hope triples (the other nine indicators fixed by the appendix's own codes) gives scaled chisq 77.7271 / TLI 0.94969 / CFI 0.96189 / RMSEA 0.04156 for {hope1, hope4, hope5} against the published 77.727 / .950 / .962 / .042; the nearest rival triple is {2,3,4} at 80.585 / .940 / .955, 2.86 away in chisq. (C2) ORDER WITHIN THAT TRIPLE: Fig 1 prints the standardized loadings box by box as SHS1 .60, SHS4 .67, SHS5 .81 with residuals .64, .56, .34; the reproduced model gives hope1 0.597, hope4 0.667, hope5 0.814 and residuals 0.644, 0.555, 0.338 -- every one matching to two decimals. A hope1<->hope5 swap would read .81/.67/.60 against the printed .60/.67/.81, so the two pathways items in the triple are separated individually. hope3 then follows by elimination: (B) puts it in pathways {1,3,5} and (C1) excludes it from the CPC-12 pair {1,5}. NOT ESTABLISHED: hope2 vs hope6. Both are agency items (B), neither entered the CPC-12 (C1), their item means are 4.3645 and 4.3302 and their mean correlations with the other five columns 0.492 and 0.494, and no per-item statistic for SHS2 or SHS6 is published for this sample. Swapping them leaves every number above unchanged. Four of six items are distinguished from every other item; two are not. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

route: 3 (published subscale totals) + 5 (subscale block structure) + 4/CFA (parameter implied by the item text) + 6 (keying polarity)
evidence: Four routes against the PLOS S1 Dataset (321 x 76) and the paper's Tables 1-2, all re-run by verify_lorenz_2016_optimism2.R. (A) INSTRUMENT: optimism2's six non-filler columns give M=4.406 / alpha=.736 against Table 1's published LOT-R 4.41/.74, while optimism1's five columns give 4.827/.819 against the published AFF 4.83/.82 -- optimism2 is the LOT-R, not the AFF. (B) SCORED SET: of all 210 six-column subsets, {1,3,4,7,9,10} minimises |M-4.41|+|alpha-.74| at 0.0083; the runner-up {2,3,4,5,9,10} is 0.0774, 9.4x worse. This fixes the fillers at optimism2.2/.5/.6/.8, matching Glaesmer et al.'s 'Die Items 2, 5, 6 und 8 sind Fuellitems'. (C) OPTIMISM/PESSIMISM SPLIT: of the 10 ways to halve those six, {1,4,10} vs {3,7,9} maximises block cohesion (mean within-block r .394 vs cross-block .266, gap .128; next-best partition {1,4,9}/{3,7,10} gaps only .070), matching the canonical assignment. (D) ITEM 10: substituting each optimism2 column in turn as the third indicator of the CPC-12 optimism facet, optimism2.10 gives chisq=77.727, df=50, TLI=.950, CFI=.962, RMSEA=.042 -- the paper's published values to three decimals -- against 82.690 for the next-best column (optimism2.9). This is the column the S1 Appendix labels LOT-R10. (E) POLARITY: the six scored columns as stored give alpha .736 (published .74) while recoding 3/7/9 as the LOT-R manual directs gives -0.015, and the pessimism columns correlate +.266 on average with the optimism columns, so items 3/7/9 are stored ALREADY reverse-coded and their option_text is inverted accordingly. NOT ESTABLISHED, which is why this is PARTIAL: optimism2.1 vs optimism2.4 (both optimism items, identical under every route above, and neither Glaesmer et al. 2008 nor Lorenz et al. 2016 publishes per-item LOT-R statistics); the order within {3,7,9}; and the order within the fillers {2,6,8} (optimism2.5 is separated from them by its mean of 5.10, the highest of the ten, but 2/6/8 sit at 3.61/3.71/3.90 and are not distinguished). So the routes pin the filler set, the optimism/pessimism split, item 10 and the stored direction, not every item against every other item.

route: 7 (marker item, cross-instrument) + 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution) + 3 (published total)
evidence: Cross-instrument content correlations over all 1296 wave-1 respondents (verify_lu_2017_gad7.R): corr(GAD_i, PHQ_8), the PHQ-9's only psychomotor-restlessness item, is highest for GAD_5 at 0.449 against 0.246/0.300/0.292/0.304/0.337/0.254 for GAD_1/2/3/4/6/7, and PHQ_8 is reciprocally GAD_5's strongest PHQ-9 correlate (0.449, next 0.433 PHQ_7, then 0.332 0.317 0.304 0.283 0.260 0.248 0.209). GAD_6 is the strongest correlate of PSS_9, the PSS-10 anger item (0.321 vs 0.275 0.290 0.261 0.222 0.203 0.203). Item means 0.666 (GAD_1) > 0.535 > 0.471 > 0.391 > 0.384 > 0.215 (GAD_5) > 0.175 (GAD_7) corroborate: restlessness and fear-of-something-awful lowest, the usual community-sample pattern. Option axis separately settled by the instrument: the GAD-7 form prints 0/1/2/3 beside its four anchors, and in the deposit the sheet's own GAD7 total equals the raw sum of GAD_1..GAD_7 exactly (max abs diff 0.0), mean 2.84 SD 2.87 range 0-17 against the paper's published 2.8 +/- 2.9 (a flipped coding would give 18.2), so items are stored raw and unreversed. NOT ESTABLISHED: this route pins GAD_5 and GAD_6 only; GAD_1, GAD_2, GAD_3, GAD_4 and GAD_7 are not distinguished from one another, because none has a comparably specific content twin in the PHQ-9 or PSS-10; the PSS_9 leg additionally assumes the deposit's PSS_1..PSS_10 are in canonical PSS-10 order. Hence PARTIAL.
